Tick for a machine homed to its back-left corner, where the table lies at negative Y - the artwork's TOP-left corner goes on the origin and the job runs toward the front. Clear it for an ordinary work origin at the front-left of the stock, where the job runs toward the back.
Repeat the same artwork across a fixture, each copy a pitch further on than the one before. One drawing stays the single source of the shape.
Pitch is signed. On a back-left origin the table lies at negative Y, so stacking copies front-to-back needs a negative Pitch Y.

Untick for a dry run: the head follows the entire path at the same feeds, so you can watch where the job lands, but every S word is 0 and the laser is never enabled. Not remembered between imports - it comes back ticked every time.
Step the power up on each copy to burn a test strip: the same artwork at rising exposure, in one job, on one piece of material. Leave at 0 for every copy the same.
Added to the outline power for each copy after the first. 50 with a power of 200 gives 200, 250, 300... Negative ramps down.
